newsitem.title: GERMANY: German paper says Bonn mulls raising '97 borrowing.
newsitem.headline: German paper says Bonn mulls raising '97 borrowing.

text.p: German newspaper Berliner Morgenpost reported on Wednesday that the Bonn government is considering raising its net borrowing target this year, despite efforts to trim back government debt before currency union.
For 1997, the Bonn government has allowed itself 53.4 billion marks for its budget defict.

In its Wednesday edition the Morgenpost said the government was considering a "measured" increase in net borrowing, adding that unnamed government sources had said Finance Minister Theo Waigel would present a package of possible measures to close the gaps in the 1997 budget on Thursday evening.
Finance Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.
Talk about Germany's budget gap has taken on special meaning as Bonn scrambles to ready itself for European currency union, scheduled to begin in 1999.
The newspaper also said the government would scrap discussed plans to possibly raise the mineral oil tax in light of heavy opposition from the junior coalition partners Free Democrats.
The newspaper added that Germany's membership in Europe's currency union would not be jeopardised if Bonn's 1997 budget deficit were slightly above 3.0 percent.
